section_summary: This section contains correspondence about cargo discharged from the Sanyo Maru, reports on Japanese shipping and shipbuilding, and documents establishing the requisitioned status of the Tatuta Maru. It also includes a wartime shipping survey prepared in Kobe and certified extracts from 1938 consular reports tracing the growth of Japanese government control over merchant shipping.

subfiles.title: Netherlands Ambassador's inquiry about Sanyo Maru cargo
subfiles.about: Requests value, whereabouts, and sale proceeds of cargo discharged from the Sanyo Maru in New York.
subfiles.summary: The ambassador seeks records for the Netherlands Shipping and Trading Committee in London.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Netherlands cargo inquiry
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the July 10 inquiry and reports its referral to appropriate authorities.
subfiles.summary: The inquiry was referred to appropriate United States authorities.

subfiles.title: Referral of Sanyo Maru cargo inquiry to Treasury
subfiles.about: Forwards the Netherlands request for information about Sanyo Maru cargo.
subfiles.summary: State asks Treasury to provide the requested cargo information.

subfiles.title: Treasury acknowledgment of cargo inquiry
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the request and promises a fuller reply once information is secured.
subfiles.summary: Treasury says the Sanyo Maru inquiry is receiving active attention.

subfiles.title: State Department follow-up to Treasury
subfiles.about: Forwards a renewed Netherlands inquiry about the availability of Sanyo Maru cargo information.
subfiles.summary: State sends Treasury the ambassador's September 18 follow-up.

subfiles.title: British Survey article on Japan's merchant marine
subfiles.about: Transmits a British Survey article and checks its claims about Japanese shipbuilding capacity and methods.
subfiles.summary: Somerville reports A. C. Hardy's estimate of roughly 500,000 annual tons, with no confirmed assembly-line methods; welding remained possible.

subfiles.title: Grew despatch transmitting Tatuta Maru documents
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy Tokyo
subfiles.about: Transmits Japanese documents establishing the requisition and government supervision of the Tatuta Maru.
subfiles.summary: The despatch lists a Foreign Office note, requisition order, inspectors' embarkation order, and six officer appointments.

subfiles.title: Japanese Foreign Office note on Tatuta Maru
subfiles.about: Announces the government's decision to requisition Tatuta Maru for passenger service to Los Angeles and Balboa.
subfiles.summary: The note forwards the requisition and related orders under the bilateral understanding.

subfiles.title: Embarkation order for Tatuta Maru supervisors
subfiles.about: Orders two officials to take delivery of Tatuta Maru and supervise its voyage.
subfiles.summary: The order identifies two government supervisors for the requisitioned ship.

subfiles.title: Appointment of Fumio Takiura
subfiles.about: Appoints Takiura to passenger and mail business on a requisitioned vessel.
subfiles.summary: Takiura is assigned to passenger and mail transport business.

subfiles.title: Appointment of Yukitsugu Yanagisawa
subfiles.about: Appoints Yanagisawa to passenger and mail business on a requisitioned vessel.
subfiles.summary: Yanagisawa is assigned to passenger and mail transport business.

subfiles.title: Appointment of Kazuo Kurimura
subfiles.about: Appoints Kurimura to passenger and mail business on a requisitioned vessel.
subfiles.summary: Kurimura is assigned to passenger and mail transport business.

subfiles.title: Appointment of Sho Kato
subfiles.about: Appoints Kato to passenger and mail business on a requisitioned vessel.
subfiles.summary: Kato is assigned to passenger and mail transport business.

subfiles.title: Appointment of Takeo Ishikawa
subfiles.about: Appoints Ishikawa to passenger and mail business on a requisitioned vessel.
subfiles.summary: Ishikawa is assigned to passenger and mail transport business.

subfiles.title: Appointment of Shohei Kimura
subfiles.about: Appoints Kimura to passenger and mail business on a requisitioned vessel.
subfiles.summary: Kimura is assigned to passenger and mail transport business.

subfiles.title: Tatuta Maru requisition order and sailing schedule
subfiles.about: Requisitions Tatuta Maru for government-directed passenger and mail transport between Japan, Los Angeles, and Balboa.
subfiles.summary: The order requires the company to conduct the voyage under embarked government supervisors. It regulates schedule changes, passenger boarding, cargo, and accounting. The appended schedule gives December departures and arrivals at Yokohama, Los Angeles, and Balboa.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs note on Japanese shipping losses
subfiles.about: Highlights loss estimates in the attached wartime shipping report.
subfiles.summary: The note suggests Japanese merchant losses substantially exceeded 250,000 tons.

subfiles.title: Forwarding despatch for Japanese wartime shipping report
subfiles.about: Forwards Roy Melbourne's report prepared during internment at Kobe.
subfiles.summary: The report draws on printed material and Melbourne's observations of Kobe shipping.

subfiles.title: Japanese Wartime Shipping: December 1941 to June 1942
subfiles.about: Surveys Japanese wartime shipping control, shipbuilding, transport capacity, companies, losses, and labor.
subfiles.summary: Melbourne traces the consolidation of merchant shipping under state management and the growing authority of the Navy and Communications Ministry over yards, materials, labor, and vessel operations. He discusses ambitious construction targets, standard ship types, financing, occupied shipyards, and shortages. The report also assesses captured tonnage, probable understated shipping losses, company mergers, and the use of American prisoners as stevedores.

subfiles.title: Netherlands follow-up on Sanyo Maru cargo
subfiles.about: Requests expedited consideration of the Netherlands inquiry into Sanyo Maru cargo.
subfiles.summary: The ambassador asks State to press the relevant authorities for a decision.

subfiles.title: London despatch on Japanese shipbuilding methods
subfiles.about: Forwards confidential Lloyd's Register evidence about welding and potential Japanese yard output.
subfiles.summary: Lloyd's surveyors observed significant Japanese use of welding before 1939. Charles W. Spray had no later reliable evidence but estimated that welding and assembly methods might raise capacity by 20 percent if materials and labor allowed.

subfiles.title: Lloyd's Register surveyors' statements on Japanese welding
subfiles.from: Charles W. Spray and Lloyd's Register surveyors
subfiles.about: Records surveyors' observations of welding and their limited knowledge of prefabrication in Japanese yards.
subfiles.summary: McGlashan, Garnett, and Buchanan describe widespread welding equipment and training before 1939, including naval construction. They provide no evidence of assembly-line ship production.

subfiles.title: Tumulty letter listing Japanese vessel owners
subfiles.about: Identifies the companies owning vessels listed in an earlier June 5 letter.
subfiles.summary: Tumulty supplies a list of Japanese tanker, shipping, and trading companies.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Tumulty's shipping-information request
subfiles.about: Seeks clearance to provide Tumulty extracts from Kobe consular reports.
subfiles.summary: Burke notes incomplete records and asks whether certified extracts may be furnished.

subfiles.title: Record of certified extracts furnished to Tumulty
subfiles.about: Records delivery of certified shipping-report extracts to Tumulty.
subfiles.summary: Certified copies were furnished July 20; no formal reply was made.

subfiles.title: Duplicate record of certified extracts furnished to Tumulty
subfiles.about: Repeats the record of extracts supplied to Tumulty.
subfiles.summary: A duplicate note records delivery of certified copies and no formal reply.

subfiles.title: Extract from Shipping in the Japanese Empire During February 1938
subfiles.from: William E. Yuni, American Vice Consul Kobe
subfiles.about: Describes a depression in Japanese deep-sea shipping and rising operating costs.
subfiles.summary: Cargoes reportedly filled only about half of most ships' capacity, while operating costs rose about 30 percent. The extract discusses losses on South American routes and possible centralized allocation of shipping.

subfiles.title: Extract from Shipping in the Japanese Empire During March 1938
subfiles.from: William E. Yuni, American Vice Consul Kobe
subfiles.about: Describes a proposal to supervise Japanese oil tankers through the Petroleum Association.
subfiles.summary: The proposed tanker controls aimed to stabilize oil freight rates.

subfiles.title: Extract from Shipping in the Japanese Empire During April 1938
subfiles.from: William C. Affeld Jr., American Vice Consul Kobe
subfiles.about: Lists April ship launchings and discusses a proposed unified company for China services.
subfiles.summary: The extract names four launched vessels and their builders and owners. It reports plans to combine major Japanese lines' China services to respond more quickly to shifts in tonnage demand.

subfiles.title: Extract from Shipping in the Japanese Empire During July 1938
subfiles.from: William C. Affeld Jr., American Vice Consul Kobe
subfiles.about: Reports government pressure for lower rates and tighter control of Japanese shipping.
subfiles.summary: Government officials threatened direct control because voluntary bodies could not reliably limit rates or distribute tonnage. The report outlines proposed reforms, including a shipping guild, shipbuilding law, subsidies, and expanded finance. It also records charter-rate decisions for smaller vessels.

subfiles.title: Extract from Shipping in the Japanese Empire During August 1938
subfiles.from: William C. Affeld Jr., American Vice Consul Kobe
subfiles.about: Reports August launchings and the growing likelihood of direct government control.
subfiles.summary: The extract lists five launched ships and describes owners' attempts to lower rates and broaden voluntary control. It explains why costs, subsidies, finance, and limits on foreign charters made direct government control increasingly likely.

subfiles.title: Extract from Shipping in the Japanese Empire During September 1938
subfiles.from: William C. Affeld Jr., American Vice Consul Kobe
subfiles.about: Reviews steps toward shipping control, foreign-charter limits, Dairen congestion, and lighter shortages.
subfiles.summary: Shipowners' groups lowered some rates while the government prepared broader shipping and shipbuilding controls. Officials sought to reduce foreign-chartered tonnage, and owners shifted vessels among routes as Dairen became congested. The extract also outlines proposed changes to cargo handling and lighter services; its discussion continues beyond page 320.
